# Iteration 11: alignment notes

Stage: Align (Bald-Eagle-Iteration). Nothing is decided or built yet.

## Goal, in Lucas's words
"EVERY SINGLE REEL THAT IS GENERATED BY THIS SYSTEM IS ABSOLUTELY POSTABLE WITH OUT HUMAN INTERVENTION."

- Rebuilding reels: "the ONLY thing that matters is getting the system to a point where it can autonomously produce a good reel".
- Stories: "A company CANNOT be the central player of a story." "Stories need to be told through people."
- Code frames: "my reaction was a little premature." "The reel honestly wasn't BAD. It just wasn't as good as we needed it to be."
- Decision pending: "revert back to the old system, flip the hybrid model ... or continue building this way", after a deep dive.
- Creative pass: "getting the creativity engine to be a little more eager (in the last reel it didn't do a single thing)".

- The creative pass returned empty lists. Its prompt says "Empty lists are a good answer", and it can only add, from one still per frame.
- Detection mostly works; repair mostly doesn't: design problems 14 → 12 with some new; measured problems 36 → 38, then 33 → 29.
- Every check ends in a flag. No flag can stop delivery.
- Frame 8's black dot traces by code reading to `kit/components/stage.js:512`, the one-colour logo filter. Not yet re-run.
- Director: $6.78 of $9.83, of which $4.22 is follow-up rounds.

## Open
- Revert, flip or keep building.
- "Never block a reel" against "every reel postable".

## Decisions (2026-11-05)
- **Never held back.** Asked whether a reel with serious faults should be held: "No. They should never be held back." So postability has to come from repair.
- **The creative pass becomes a problem solver and can change frames.** "The creative pass should ABSOLUTELY be able to change frames!" "it's looking at these frames that were just put together with code and it's supposed to see what's weak and then change around whatever it needs to to make it strong." "It's not JUST a creative pass. It's a PROBLEM SOLVER! When frames are wrong/bad, it is able to figure out how to make them good!" "the new frame worker" should "operate at the highest ability possible."
- **The diagram matches his picture of the system.**
- **Dynamic screenshots across the whole chain.** "build code that dynamically decides where all the screenshots need to happen so that everything is caught."

## Screenshots today (checked in code)
- Model reviewers: design review gets one settled still per frame, plus the first instant. The first viewer gets a contact sheet of the same moments. The creative pass gets one still per frame.
- Measured checks: every 0.2 s in a browser (`kit/screen.mjs`), which reads geometry and doesn't judge the picture.
- The every-3-seconds stills were my own audit method, not the system's.

## Screenshot proposal (for the build)
Code derives capture moments from each frame's timeline: first instant, each arrival once settled, each mark, label or speech landing, each camera stop, each exit, the last moment, and any time a measured check reports. Near-identical stills are dropped. Estimated review cost: about $0.50 a read, against $0.11 today.

## Conflicts this creates
- Reverses "No model writes frame code" (MD-153) if the solver may write frame code.
- Bends "model states intent, code does geometry" ([[right-first-time-over-review-gates]]).
- "One fix, then flag" ([[explainers-never-block]]) can't deliver postable reels; repair needs more rounds.

## Decisions, round 2 (2026-11-05)
- **Composite, don't drop.** "Near-identical stills shouldn't get dropped. Instead, they should get composited." "compositing should become the NEW NORM." Replaces the "dropped" line in the screenshot proposal above.
- **Solver power: B.** It can edit the plan, set any piece's exact size and position, and write custom code for a frame. Measured checks are feedback it must answer; they can't silently remove its work.
- **The director keeps its fixes.** "the director should be able to fix stuff before the solver sees anything." Wanted: cheaper director passes without moving the job to the solver.
- **Solver rounds.** "2 per frame, sonnet for first round and then opus if it requires a second pass. $4 limit, I like the last resort plan." Last resort: the frame's simplest clean version, flagged.

## Compositing today (checked in code)
- First viewer: already a contact sheet, 270x480 tiles.
- Design review: separate 720x1280 stills, about 1,230 tokens each.
- Creative pass: separate stills, no compositing.
- Plan: one labelled sheet per frame (1x2, 2x2, 3x2, 3x3 by moment count), tiles about 441 wide. A 6-moment sheet is about 2,770 tokens, about 62% less per moment. A frame with too many moments gets a second sheet instead of smaller tiles. The solver also gets a full-size still of the frame it is editing. Estimated review read: about $0.25, against $0.11 today, seeing about 6x the moments. Legibility of small text at this size is unproven until a live run.

## Why director fixes cost what they do (job 7e9fcc49)
- The whole plan is only about 8k tokens, yet the fix rounds wrote 70k, 18k and 22k tokens on Opus at high effort. The ledger can't split thinking from resubmissions.
- Variety and image check run as separate fix rounds.
- The prompt demands the whole plan back, and `validateFixedPlan` then discards every frame the fix didn't name.

## Cheaper director fixes (proposed; rough target $1-1.50 against $4.22, not measured)
1. One combined pre-build fix round for variety and image check.
2. Return, and send, only the named frames.
3. Lower effort on fixes.
4. Possibly Sonnet first, Opus if still failing (open).

## Decisions, round 3 (2026-11-05)
Lucas: "1 yes, 2 split them like you said, 3 every frame".
- Director fixes use the ladder: Sonnet first, Opus if the problem persists.
- Rendered-frame findings are split. Content faults (wrong or missing picture, missing focus) go to the director once. Layout faults go straight to the solver.
- The solver takes one reel-wide look at every frame and picks what is wrong or weak, flagged or not. Its prompt drops every "doing nothing is good" line.

## Decisions, round 4 (2026-11-05)
Lucas: "1 yes, 2 yes, 3 no, I've already said I'm fine with these running up to 80 seconds!"
- The proposed flow is approved.
- The solver may not touch the script, voice, facts or frame length, may use any harvested picture, may order drawings, and doesn't search the web.
- No length work. Reels may run up to 80 s.

## Decisions, round 5 (2026-11-05)
Lucas approved the extra renders, the solver prompts and the build: "start the build". His direction for the solver, now in the prompts: "reconsider what is shown vs. what could be shown"; "visibility into the full arsenal of frame types"; "something that is uniquely apt for that scene that builds on the assets it has with out try to do too much"; "really good at knowing what kinds of upgrades to make that will land with a high rate of success, based on the harness".
